result.text:
The new version is built in the image and all **45 tests pass**. Here is the design.

## Model (`SurveyCrawler` category)

**`SurveyCrawler`** — knows `position`, `facing`, the `sonar` it senses with and the `run` it is processing commands in. `process:` interprets a `ReadStream` of characters, guarded by a handler that aborts the run and passes the error on:

```smalltalk
process: aSequenceOfCommands
	[ self processCommandsIn: (ReadStream on: aSequenceOfCommands) ]
		on: Error
		do: [ :anError | self abortRun. anError pass ]
```

**`CrawlerFacing`** (Up/Down/Left/Right) — now answers `advanceDisplacement`, `retreatDisplacement`, `clockwise` and `counterClockwise` instead of mutating the crawler; facings became values, which is what undoing a turn needs.

**`CrawlerSonar`** — `detecting: { 1@3 -> BoulderGround new }`, answering `FirmSandGround` for every position it was not told about.

**`SeabedGround`** — `FirmSandGround` moves by the displacement asked for; `BoulderGround` signals on both `displacementFor:during:` and `turn:to:`; `SiltGround` asks the run for the slide displacement and turns as firm sand does. The silt's slide distance comes from a generator (a `Random` in production), so tests are not at the mercy of chance.

**`CrawlerRun`** — `CrawlerNormalRun` slides on silt, ignores undo actions and starts guarded runs; `CrawlerGuardedRun` collects undo actions, refuses silt, refuses a nested run and refuses to be left unfinished. No `if` decides any of this.

**`CrawlerCommand`** — `CrawlerCommand for: $a` answers the command for a character; each one is executed with the previous command and answers the one to remember, so a `CrawlerRepetitionCommand` (a digit) just tells the previous command to `repeat: digit + 2`. `CrawlerNoCommand` is the null object that makes `'0'`, `'a00'` and `'(a)0'` invalid, and `CrawlerRepeatableCommand` is what tells `a t h g` apart from `( )`.

Undoing is done by doing the opposite movement: `displaceBy:` registers `[ position := position - aDisplacement ]` with the run. `abortRun` replaces the interrupted run before undoing it — that is the one place with a comment, since the dependency is invisible otherwise.

## Tests (`SurveyCrawler-Tests`)

The 16 original tests still pass unchanged except for the two that name error descriptions, which moved to the class that signals them (`CrawlerCommand`, `CrawlerFacing`). 29 new tests cover repetition (including every invalid place a digit can appear), boulders when advancing, retreating and turning, silt sliding forward and backward plus its maximum distance and that it does not affect turning, and guarded runs: success, undo of movements, of turns and of repeated movements, silt and invalid commands inside them, nesting, unfinished runs, `)` without `(`, several runs in one sequence, a finished run not being undone by a later failure, and the crawler still working after a run failed.

Two things worth your judgement: a digit after `(` or `)` is treated as an invalid command (the spec only says repetition applies to `a t h g`), and on silt the sonar is consulted only for the cell the command aims at, not for the cells the crawler slides across. The image is saved; the package has no file name, so nothing was written to disk.
